profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: The Belynich image was venerated by both Orthodox and Roman Catholics. The OCA traces changes in custody around the Mogilev district and the monastery at Belynich.

blocks.text: The selected historic panel shows Mary crowned and holding the crowned Child. She carries a sceptre; Christ holds an orb. Its bright garments and developed royal attributes belong to this eighteenth- or nineteenth-century depiction. The file identifies its museum setting at Mogilev; it is not asserted to be the first image in the shrine’s history.

blocks.text: The OCA connects the icon’s Catholic custody with the period following the 1596 Unia and a monastery founded in 1622–1624 by Lev Sapega. It records the monastery’s dissolution in 1832 and the subsequent status of the church as a parish. These details describe the received institutional history of the shrine, not the individual painter or manufacture date of the displayed museum panel.

blocks.text: The account marks April 12, 1876 with the first Orthodox Liturgy after the monastery’s restoration. Its account of shared veneration and later Orthodox custody should not be treated as an assertion that both communions endorse every theological claim about icons or church authority. The commemorative history identifies this image’s place in the devotional life of the region.
